concepts.title: Java Basics and Syntax
concepts.description: Learn Java fundamentals, variables, and data types

teachingContent.intermediate:
Java's type system and variable declarations:

**Primitive Data Types:**
```java
byte b = 127;           // 8-bit: -128 to 127
short s = 32000;        // 16-bit: -32,768 to 32,767
int i = 2147483647;     // 32-bit: -2^31 to 2^31-1
long l = 9223372036854775807L; // 64-bit

float f = 3.14f;        // 32-bit decimal
double d = 3.14159;     // 64-bit decimal (default)

boolean flag = true;    // true or false
char c = 'A';           // 16-bit Unicode character
```

**Type Casting:**
```java
// Implicit (widening)
int num = 100;
double d = num; // Automatic

// Explicit (narrowing)
double price = 19.99;
int rounded = (int) price; // 19
```

**Constants:**
```java
final double PI = 3.14159;
final int MAX_SIZE = 100;
// Cannot be changed after initialization
```
teachingContent.advanced:
Advanced type concepts and best practices:

**Wrapper Classes:**
```java
// Primitive vs Wrapper
int primitive = 10;
Integer wrapper = 10; // Autoboxing

// Useful methods
Integer.parseInt("123");    // String to int
Integer.toString(123);      // int to String
Integer.MAX_VALUE;          // 2147483647
```

**Type Inference (Java 10+):**
```java
var name = "John";      // String
var age = 25;           // int
var price = 19.99;      // double
// Type inferred from right side
```

**Best Practices:**
- Use `int` for whole numbers (default)
- Use `double` for decimals (default)
- Use `final` for constants
- Use meaningful variable names
- Follow camelCase convention

concepts.title: Arrays and Collections
concepts.description: Learn to work with arrays and collections

teachingContent.advanced:
Advanced collections and streams:

**Streams (Java 8+):**
```java
List<Integer> numbers = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3, 4, 5);

// Filter and map
List<Integer> doubled = numbers.stream()
    .filter(n -> n % 2 == 0)
    .map(n -> n * 2)
    .collect(Collectors.toList());
// [4, 8]
```

**HashSet (Unique elements):**
```java
HashSet<String> set = new HashSet<>();
set.add("Apple");
set.add("Banana");
set.add("Apple"); // Duplicate ignored
System.out.println(set.size()); // 2
```

**Sorting:**
```java
Arrays.sort(numbers);              // Arrays
Collections.sort(list);            // Lists
list.sort(Comparator.reverseOrder()); // Reverse
```
